title: Ivy and the Lost Robin
markdown:
High up in the Cloudneedle Mountains, where clouds tickle the very tops of the trees and whisper secrets to the little flowers, lived a young witch named Ivy. Her cottage wasn't spooky at all! It was as cozy as a warm hug. Its roof was made of soft moss that smelled like wet dirt and summer rain. The windows were round and cheerful, twinkling like fallen stars. They showed the happy glow of Ivy’s own warm fireplace.

Ivy wasn't a witch who made bubbling potions or cast dark spells. Her magic was gentle. It helped daisy chains grow extra long for happy children. It made her teacups magically refill with warm, sweet tea.

One sunny afternoon, the kind where sunbeams danced like happy sprites on the ground, Ivy was in her garden. She was trying to teach a shy mushroom to dance. This mushroom was plump, with a cap the colour of a ripe plum. It only wiggled its cap just a little bit. "Hmph," Ivy said, wiggling her eyebrows. "You're a bit shy, aren't you? But that little wiggle is a big success!"

Then, with the happy buzzing of bees and the soft sigh of the wind in the pine trees, she heard a tiny, sad chirp. "Hmm," Ivy wondered, her bright, twilight-coloured hair shimmering as she tilted her head. "What's that little sound? It sounds so sad."

Curiosity pulled her like a soft string. She followed the sound. Her soft boots crunched on the pine needles. She found it near a fluffy cloud-bush. It looked as soft as spun sugar. There, sitting on the ground, was a very small, very confused robin. Its feathers were the warm colour of a summer sunset. Its bright, round eyes looked lost and a little sad.

"Oh, you poor little darling!" Ivy whispered. Her smile was as bright as a new candle. She scooped up the robin very gently. Her hands cupped its tiny body. It felt as light as a puff of dandelion fluff. "Are you lost, little one?"

Just then, a familiar 'caw-caw' called from above. It was Corvus, Ivy's best crow friend. He was sleek and smart, with eyes like shiny black stones. He always watched over her. His dark wings rustled like paper as he landed softly on her shoulder. "Caw-caw! Little bird needs help?" he croaked. His voice sounded like smooth pebbles rolling in a quiet stream.

"Yes, Corvus," Ivy said softly. Her voice was full of kindness as she looked at the little robin in her hands. "This little robin is all alone. It looks quite worried."

Corvus tilted his head. His clever eyes looked at the little bird. "Night is coming," he croaked. His voice was serious, but not scary. "Robin needs to be home. Safe home. Warm home."

Ivy nodded. Her heart felt a little worried for the tiny bird. She knew Corvus was right. The sun, so high and bright, was starting to dip behind the mountain peaks. The sky turned soft shades of peach and gentle purple. "Don't you worry, little robin," she whispered. She stroked its soft feathers. "We'll help you. We'll find your home before the moon is high up."

So, with the little robin tucked safely in the special pocket of her apron, and Corvus fluttering beside her like a dark guardian, Ivy set off. They walked deeper into the whispering pines. The tall trees stood quiet and strong. Their needles sighed a soft song in the gentle breeze. The path ahead began to get dimmer. The shadows stretched and played hide-and-seek among the tree trunks. But Ivy’s heart was bright with the warm glow of hope.

"It's getting a little bit dim now, isn't it?" Ivy said softly. She was just noticing. The dimness was just part of the day turning into evening. Corvus gave a comforting 'caw' from his perch on her shoulder.

"Don't worry, little one," Corvus croaked. "We know these paths. They are our friends."

But then, as they walked around a big, mossy rock that looked like a sleeping giant, they saw something surprising and lovely. It was a trail of tiny, sparkling dewdrops. Each one shone like a little diamond. It led off the main path into some soft ferns. Standing by this sparkly dewdrop path was a little elf. He had a smile as wide and cheerful as a moon cookie. He was no bigger than Ivy’s hand. His ears were shaped like the tips of new green leaves. He wore a waistcoat woven from the softest, shiniest moonbeams.

"Hello there!" chirped the elf. His voice sounded like tiny silver bells tinkling. "I'm Pip! Are you looking for the way? I know these mountains like the back of my hand – or rather, the back of my ear!" Pip wiggled one of his pointed ears. Corvus let out a little chuckle-caw, a sound of pure amusement.

Ivy’s eyes grew wide with delight and a little bit of wonder. "Oh, yes please!" she exclaimed. "We're helping this little robin find its home. It seems to have flown quite far."

Pip giggled. His giggle sounded like tiny wind chimes. "Ah, this little robin! It has flown a bit far from its cozy nest, hasn't it? But don't worry! This dewdrop path is a very special shortcut. It always leads to where you need to be. And I know all the secret paths and sunny clearings!"

Pip led them down the sparkling dewdrop path. It smelled faintly of sweet honeysuckle and the clean scent of fresh rain. It was much easier to see the way with the path shimmering ahead. Corvus flew in front, his dark, sleek shape a friendly shadow against the deepening twilight sky. He called out encouraging caws. Soon, they came to a small clearing. It was bathed in the soft glow of the rising moon. They heard more chirps. These weren't sad chirps. They were happy, excited chirps! There, on a sturdy branch of a grand old pine tree, were several robins. They were all calling out in a happy reunion.

"Mama! Papa!" chirped the little robin. It had been so quiet and worried. It hopped out of Ivy’s pocket, eager to fly. With a flutter of tiny wings and a flurry of happy chirps, it was back with its family. They welcomed it with little nuzzles and fond chirps. Oh, it was a sight to warm anyone’s heart!

Ivy, Corvus, and Pip watched. A gentle warmth spread through them, like sunshine on a cool day. "Hooray!" whispered Ivy. Her smile beamed. Corvus gave a contented 'caw-caw' of pure happiness. Pip clapped his tiny hands together with glee.

As the first stars began to peek out, like tiny scattered diamonds in the velvet sky, Ivy waved goodbye to the happy robin family. They chirped their thanks. She waved to Pip, who gave a cheerful wink. The walk back to her cozy cottage felt even cozier now. It was filled with the happy feeling of doing a good deed. The moon had risen fully, a soft, silvery smile in the night sky. The whispering pines seemed to be singing a gentle lullaby just for them.

"Well, Corvus," Ivy said softly, her voice a little tired but happy, as they walked hand-in-wing towards home. "That was a truly wonderful adventure."

Corvus landed on her shoulder. He nudged her cheek with his smooth head. It was a gesture of friendship. "Caw-caw. Best kind of adventure, Ivy. Helping friends. Always best."

And as Ivy snuggled into her warm, soft bed, with Corvus dozing contentedly on a cushion nearby, his dark feathers looking like a patch of night sky, she knew they had done a very good thing. The Cloudneedle Mountains, even as the night wrapped them in its gentle arms, felt safe and full of quiet, twinkling magic. And that is how a little bit of kindness, shared among friends, can make the whole world feel like the coziest, safest, happiest home.
characters: Ivy the young witch, a crow
